candidate.answerReason: The bars cost 400 dollars and bring in 500 dollars, leaving a profit of 100 dollars, matching choice A.

methods.label: Calculate cost and sales revenue
methods.explanation:
Profit is the money received from sales minus the purchase cost. Buying \(1000\) bars in groups of five gives \(1000/5=200\) groups, each costing \(2\) dollars. Selling them in pairs gives \(1000/2=500\) pairs, each bringing in \(1\) dollar. Thus, in dollars,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{Cost}&=200\cdot2=400,\\
\text{Revenue}&=500\cdot1=500.
\end{aligned}
\]
The profit is \(500-400=\boxed{100}\) dollars, choice \(\text{A}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses division into equal groups, total-price multiplication, and subtraction.

candidate.annotationRationale: The central relationship is total price equals price per group times number of groups. Division applications determine the group counts, and integer arithmetic supports the cost, revenue, and profit calculations.

review.mathematicalCheck: There are 1000/5=200 purchase groups costing $400 and 1000/2=500 sales pairs yielding $500. Profit is $500−$400=$100.
review.levelCheck: The explanation clearly distinguishes cost, revenue, and profit using elementary arithmetic.
